crime.value: Murder by paper knife stabbing. David Ostrander found dead with Penn's paper knife embedded in his throat. Central question: Who killed David—Penn (who struck him moments before), Ginnie (who had motive and opportunity), or was it a frame?
crime.quote: Something shiny was sticking out of David's throat, and Penn recognized it—the haft of his own paper knife that he'd neglected to pack.

victim.value: David Ostrander, 43-year-old science fiction writer. Killable because he manipulates those around him (Ginnie, Penn, previous employees) in cruel emotional games to bind them to him and prevent their escape.
victim.quote: Your dream gave me a splendid idea for this one...Ginnie likes these little dramas. They serve to draw us together and they keep her from getting bored.

closed_world.value: The Ostrander household in Stonebridge, New York—a domestic space where Penn has come to collect his belongings. David and Ginnie are present; Hanna the maid is also in the house.
closed_world.quote: Lights were on in the living room, and also in Ginnie's room upstairs...Penn followed her across the broad foyer.

culprit_and_motive.value: Ginnie Ostrander, David's wife. She kills David to free herself from his psychological manipulation and control, wiping the knife handle to frame Penn, whom David has now turned against her.
culprit_and_motive.quote: But it was you that wiped the handle. You were wiping it with your skirt when I came in the door.

resolution.value: Hanna's testimony exposes Ginnie as the true killer. She witnessed Ginnie wiping the knife handle after Penn struck David but before David's death, proving Ginnie's guilt and Penn's innocence.
resolution.quote: Hanna looked at her with horror. 'I'll call them, ma'am. But it was you that wiped the handle. You were wiping it with your skirt when I came in the door.'

investigator.value: Penn Knowlton, the suspect and protagonist. The reader experiences the mystery through Penn's perspective as he is falsely accused, imprisoned, released, and ultimately confronted with evidence of Ginnie's guilt.
investigator.quote: Penn stared at Ginnie. He and she were not finished with each other yet.
